title: Cofinal quotient reductions preserve constructibility and uniform Tor bounds
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $O$ and uniformizer $\pi$, and a scheme $T$. Put $R=\mathcal O_{E,T}$, $B_N=(O/\ell^N)_T$ and $D_j=(O/\pi^j)_T$ for $N,j\geq1$ [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers]. Write $\ell=u\pi^e$ with $u\in O^\times$ and $e\geq1$. For $K\in D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and $eN\geq j$, the canonical quotient $B_N\to D_j$ induces a natural scalar-associativity isomorphism in $D(D_j)$
$$\bigl(K\otimes_R^LB_N\bigr)\otimes_{B_N}^LD_j\xrightarrow{\sim}K\otimes_R^LD_j,$$
where all tensors are the target-coefficient derived change of rings of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. If $P\to K$ is a K-flat resolution with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex], then $P\otimes_RB_N$ is K-flat over $B_N$ and this isomorphism is represented by the ordinary reassociation map to $P\otimes_RD_j$, with its $D_j$-action. The comparisons are natural in $K$ and commute with further quotient maps in both indices.

Suppose there are integers $a\leq b$ such that for every $N\geq1$ the complex $K\otimes_R^LB_N$ has constructible cohomology [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf] and Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Then for every $j\geq1$, $K\otimes_R^LD_j$ has constructible cohomology and Tor amplitude in the same $[a,b]$; in particular all its cohomology sheaves outside $[a,b]$ vanish. This applies to arbitrary ramification index $e$ and arbitrary $T$; it requires no flatness or finite projective dimension of $D_j$ over $B_N$, no invertibility of $\ell$ on $T$, and no completeness assumption on $K$.

proof.text: For $eN\geq j$, the identity $\ell^N=u^N\pi^{eN}$ implies $(\ell^N)\subseteq(\pi^j)$: explicitly $\ell^N=\pi^j u^N\pi^{eN-j}$. Hence reduction of representatives defines $O/(\ell^N)\to O/(\pi^j)$ and thus $B_N\to D_j$ on the coefficient sheaves of [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers]. Its composite with $R\to B_N$ is $R\to D_j$. For $N\geq N_0$ and $j\geq j_0$ whenever the relevant quotient maps exist, all composites send the class of $x$ to the class of $x$; the quotient squares commute.

proof.text: Let $P$ be any K-flat $R$-complex, in particular the flat-term representative in the statement. For an acyclic $B_N$-complex $L$, exact restriction of scalars [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] makes $\operatorname{Res}L$ acyclic. The natural sheaf tensor cancellation of [lem-sfb-scalar-tensor-cancellation-independent], applied in each bidegree and summed with the total differential, identifies $\operatorname{Res}\operatorname{Tot}(L\otimes_{B_N}(P\otimes_R B_N))$ with $\operatorname{Tot}(\operatorname{Res}L\otimes_R P)$. The latter is acyclic by [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Exact restriction detects zero cohomology, since it retains the underlying sheaf and all underlying maps. Thus $P\otimes_R B_N$ is K-flat over $B_N$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization] to $R\to B_N\to D_j$. Its comparison is an isomorphism in the target category $D(D_j)$, not merely after forgetting coefficients. Choose a flat-term K-flat representative using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]; [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and the preceding step compute both successive extensions on it. The comparison and inverse are the ordinary chain maps $(x\otimes b)\otimes d\mapsto x\otimes\bar b d$ and $x\otimes d\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes d$. They are $D_j$-linear. The cited normalization gives independence of the representative, naturality in $K$ and in the composable ring maps, and agreement of iterated comparisons. Together with the quotient squares in step 1 this proves compatibility with further quotient maps in both indices.

proof.text: Put $H_N=K\otimes_R^L B_N$. The assumed Tor interval and [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude], tested on the degree-zero unit module $B_N$, give $\mathcal H^q(H_N)=0$ outside $[a,b]$, since $H_N\otimes_{B_N}^LB_N\cong H_N$. Thus the constructible cohomology assumption makes $H_N$ an object of the bounded finite-Tor constructible category appearing in [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor]. Fix $j\geq1$ and take $N=j$; then $eN\geq j$ because $e\geq1$. Both $O/\ell^N$ and $O/\pi^j$ are finite commutative rings killed by $\ell^N$. Clause (2) of that existing node applies to their quotient map on the arbitrary scheme $T$, giving constructible cohomology and Tor amplitude in exactly $[a,b]$ for $H_N\otimes_{B_N}^LD_j$. Transfer these properties through the $D_j$-linear comparison of step 3 to $K\otimes_R^LD_j$. Testing its Tor interval on $D_j$ itself also proves the asserted cohomology vanishing. The invoked clause has no flatness or finite-projective-dimension requirement on the coefficient map and no invertibility or completeness hypothesis.

Source: main-20261015 sk-lem-sp-tower.proof final integral-constructibility sentence, and sk-def-sp-scalar-extension-functor.proof (2),(4). sk-lem-sp-tower step 4 cites the item for exactly its conclusion. Step 1: ell^N = pi^j u^N pi^{eN-j} gives (ell^N) ⊆ (pi^j); the quotient squares commute on representatives. Elementary and correct. Step 2: exact restriction (lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction), the cancellation U(M⊗_S(S⊗_R N)) ≅ UM⊗_R N natural in both variables (lem-sfb-scalar-tensor-cancellation-independent) and K-flatness of P over R give K-flatness of P⊗B_N. Restriction detects acyclicity, so this is a valid few-line argument. Step 3: lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization holds for arbitrary ring sheaves. It gives the D(T)-isomorphism, the representative maps, and naturality in K and in the composable ring maps. Together with step 1 this gives compatibility in both indices. lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings (2) with the K-flat P⊗B_N computes the iterated extension. Step 4: testing Tor amplitude on B_N gives bounded cohomology, so H_N ∈ Dctf(O/ell^N). With N=j (e≥1), det-sp-scalar-extension-functor (2) holds for any scheme T and finite rings killed by ell^j, with no flatness or ell-invertibility needed. Its (−)_B is def-weil-pbc-constant-coefficient-scalar-extension, which is defined through lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings, so it is the same functor. Small cases checked: e=1; e=2 with N=j=1 (non-flat O/pi^2 → O/pi, fine because base change preserves Tor amplitude); e=2, N=1, j=2 (D_2=B_1); K=0. lem-coef-integral-residue-tor is not a duplicate.
